problem: Map-completion ObjectNav methods (U-Net, MAE+ViT such as SGM) generate low-quality semantic maps of unexplored regions because they ignore room context and do not fully exploit the observed map (MAE random masking loses information). Location-prediction methods learn target relations individually and need pre-built datasets.
motivation: The reliability of the long-term goal depends on the quality of the generated unknown-area map. Learning contextual object relations amounts to learning the statistical distribution of objects in rooms, so completing a map amounts to sampling from a distribution consistent with the observed region. Diffusion models are good at complex distributions and support inpainting without retraining.
key_idea: Train a DDPM on ground-truth semantic room maps, condition it on LLM-inferred room-type guidance, and use RePaint-style inpainting from the explored map to generate unknown regions whose predicted target location becomes the long-term goal.
insight: Room guidance is the main contributor: removing it drops Gibson SR from 81.23 to 73.55 and MP3D SR from 41.44 to 36.21 (Table 2). Fusion design matters: multi-scale fusion with semantic attention (M1) beats cross-attention (M2) and concatenation (M3), and removing the RF or SA modules costs about 1-2%. Map-completion IoU on the test set tracks navigation performance, and halving sampling steps (1000 to 500) cuts time by 49% for only a 2-3% loss.
method: Room guidance maps: room-segmentation channels are turned into exponentially decaying blobs around each room cluster center, with sigma set to 1/4 of the mean bounding-box side, so they act as soft priors without hard room boundaries.

Denoising network: a U-Net DDPM predicting noise from x_t, t and room guidance r. Three variants: M1 multi-scale hierarchical Room Feature Fusion plus Semantic Attention (channel and spatial), M2 cross-attention, M3 concatenation.

LLM object-room prior: chain-of-thought with positive and negative prompts gives an N×M object-to-room probability matrix V. A frontier's room type is the argmax of the distance-weighted sum of V over its n=4 nearest objects.

Map completion by inpainting: the local map is cropped, rescaled (epsilon=120%) and padded to 256×256. RePaint fixes the known region with noised local-map samples while the model generates the unknown region, and DDIM-style subsampling (T=1000, S=500) speeds sampling.

Goal selection and planning: non-zero pixels in the target channel of the generated map are mapped back to the local map as the long-term goal, with argmax discretization. If the target is absent, the nearest frontier is used. Path planning is FMM with a deterministic local policy.
Inference reduction: DAR is re-invoked only when the agent nears or deviates from its goal.

setting.backbone: U-Net DDPM (trained self-supervised) + LLM for object-room priors (used offline to build the matrix, frozen)
setting.training_data: Ground-truth semantic object and room maps from Gibson (25 train scenes, tiny split) and MP3D (56 train scenes), augmented with random rotation, scaling and cropping to 256×256; LLM object-room matrix from prompting
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D + pose, building a top-down semantic map
setting.action_space: discrete: move forward, turn left, turn right, stop; long-term goals on the map with FMM planning
setting.privileged: none at test time (ground-truth room maps used only for training the diffusion model)

numbers_note: Split labelled 'val' as the paper evaluates on Gibson and MP3D validation sets. Table 2 ablations differ slightly from Table 4 in rounding (Diff-M1 SR 81.23 / 41.44).
results: DAR(1K) reaches SR 81.2 / SPL 45.3 on Gibson and SR 41.4 / SPL 15.2 on MP3D, beating map-completion SGM (78.0/44.0 and 37.7/14.7) and location-prediction T-Diff (79.6/44.9 and 39.6/15.2). It exceeds PONI by 10.3% SR on Gibson. With 500 steps it roughly matches T-Diff.
limitations: Diffusion sampling is slow, needing acceleration and reduced invocation frequency, and it is stochastic, so navigation is non-deterministic.
Depends on LLM room-type inference from a few nearby objects, and the model falls back to frontier exploration early in navigation.
Gains over T-Diff are small (SPL is roughly equal), and the paper reports only Habitat-based simulation with no real-robot tests.
